diagnosis_verifications.diagnosis: Acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF) with prerenal AKI from over-diuresis
supporting_evidence_verified: Urine specific gravity 1.000 indicating maximal dilution
Rising creatinine 2.7 mg/dL with eGFR ~18 mL/min/1.73m2
evidence_gaps: Physical exam findings (JVP, lung crackles, edema)
Exact loop diuretic dosing over past 72h
concerns: Diagnosis conflates two concepts (ADHF and over-diuresis); ensure management addresses both

evidence_gaps: Longitudinal trend of eGFR and proteinuria

diagnosis_verifications.diagnosis: Ischemic cardiomyopathy / acute coronary syndrome (ACS) precipitating decompensation
supporting_evidence_verified: Known ischemic heart disease and age 81
concerns: Probability likely overestimated given lack of any ischemic biomarkers

diagnosis_verifications.diagnosis: Medication‑induced renal insult (ACE‑I/ARB, NSAID, SGLT2‑i, loop diuretic)
evidence_gaps: Exact medication list with doses and recent changes
concerns: Without medication details the contribution cannot be quantified

evidence_gaps: Serum direct/indirect bilirubin, ALP, GGT, AST/ALT
concerns: May be a false‑positive dipstick; low probability of true hepatobiliary disease

evidence_gaps: Serum β‑hydroxybutyrate, arterial/venous pH, anion gap
concerns: Low probability unless patient is on SGLT2‑i; metabolic acidosis data missing

evidence_gaps: Urine culture, leukocyte esterase/nitrite, fever or dysuria
concerns: No laboratory or clinical signs of infection

supporting_evidence_verified: Severe HF can cause low‑T3 syndrome (physiologically plausible)
evidence_gaps: TSH, free T4, free T3 (or total T3) levels
concerns: Not a primary driver of the acute presentation

consistency_checks.detail: All severity ≥3 laboratory abnormalities are addressed by at least one diagnosis

critical_findings_addressed: Urine ketones ≈11 mg/dL with fasting glucose 65 mg/dL
top_concerns: Missing detailed medication list (especially loop diuretic, ACE‑I/ARB, SGLT2‑i)
Absence of cardiac biomarkers and ECG to exclude ACS
Unexplained bilirubinuria requiring further hepatobiliary/hemolysis work‑up
Potential SGLT2‑i‑associated ketoacidosis without confirmatory labs
recommended_primary: Acute decompensated heart failure with prerenal AKI due to over‑diuresis
review_summary: The differential is largely appropriate; the top diagnosis is well‑supported by strong objective data. Chronic cardiorenal syndrome and medication‑induced renal injury are under‑weighted, while ACS and bilirubinuria are over‑emphasized relative to available evidence. All high‑severity findings are accounted for, but key missing data (medication list, troponin/ECG, thyroid labs, bilirubin fractions) limit definitive conclusions for several secondary possibilities.
